newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on professional sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on professional sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended slightly lower on Tuesday compared to New York's previous close on professional selling, some sparked by a weakening Australian dollar, bullion traders said.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$341.80/342.30 on Tuesday compared to New York's previous close at US$342.40/90 on Monday.
"The only interesting feature was some selling because of a lower Aussie dollar," said one bullion trader.
The Australian dollar slipped to 16-month lows on Tuesday and by 0645 GMT was face down at US$0.7480/85, having slid from US$0.7513/18 late on Monday.
Gold volumes were small, so that even small trades tended to move the market, some bullion traders said.
Physical demand had quietened compared to Monday as spot prices edged higher, dealers said.
Local tael gold ended HK$6 higher at HK$3,161.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -8.00 from its previous fix at -5.00.
